_comments: Declares Journal Entries -> Journal Entry Lines as a related-record collection (MJ 6.1).
CodeGen reads RelatedRecordCollection and emits a typed `Lines` accessor onto the GENERATED
entity class, so both tiers get it. That replaces the hand-rolled collection on
JournalEntryEntityServer — `_lines`, `_deletedLines`, AddLine, RemoveLine, CreateLine and
LoadLines — which existed only on the server, so the Angular JE editor had to reach through a
service layer to compose an entry it could not model directly.
This is the case MJ's own documentation uses as the worked example for a cross-record
invariant: debits must equal credits, validated over the complete set before the first row is
written. Declared here, that check runs in the BROWSER too.
RelatedEntity and RelatedEntityJoinField are deliberately NOT set here — they are already
columns on this same row (Journal Entry Lines / JournalEntryID). Duplicating them would create
two sources of truth with the JSON copy winning silently.
Sequence maintains LineNumber, which UQ_JournalEntryLine_JE_LineNumber requires to be unique
per entry and the column requires to be NOT NULL.
Keyed by entity NAMES rather than the row's ID: EntityRelationship IDs are minted by CodeGen,
so a hardcoded UUID would stop matching the first time the database is rebuilt from zero.
Declares Journal Entry Lines -> Journal Entry Line Dimensions as a related-record collection.
WHY. `JournalEntryLineEntityServer` hand-rolled this: `_dimensions`, `_deletedDimensions`,
AddDimension / RemoveDimension / CreateDimension, plus save and delete ordering written by hand.
It was the last of that pattern in this repo, and it was SERVER-ONLY — which is why the JE
workspace keeps its dimension picks in a component Map and maps them into the operation contract
instead of putting them on the line where they belong.
No Sequence: a line's dimension tags are a SET, not an ordered list. UQ_JELDimension_Line_Dimension
already enforces one value per dimension per line, and stamping an order onto them would invent a
meaning the schema does not have.

_comments: Declares Journal Entry Batches -> Journal Entries as a READ-ONLY related-record collection.
WHY READ-ONLY, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A LIMITATION. `JournalEntryBatchEntityServer` already said
this in a comment — 'READ-ONLY by convention: mutating members happens through their own
entities / the engine — the batch never writes other aggregates outside its sanctioned
lock-release'. A convention in a comment is enforced by whoever read it. `ReadOnly: true` and
OnRemove 'refuse' make the collection say no instead.
It replaces `_members`, a hand-rolled lazy cache with its own forceRefresh flag and its own
invalidation — which is `Load(force)` and `IsLoaded` with extra steps, written once per aggregate
and wrong in a different way each time.
